items.title: Albert Murray interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 24, 1997
items.q: Tim Hicks participated briefly in the interview.

ctx.x: For the last 25 years, Albert Murray has been one of America’s most influential writers. From his first book The Omni Americans (1970) to his current The Seven League Boots, Mr. Murray has provided a unique perspective on American culture. In Stomping the Blues (1976) he offered a compelling paradigm for the importance of jazz and blues in America and his ten year collaboration with Count Basie resulted in Basie’s definitive biography Good Morning Blues. Mr. Murray has acted as a mentor to a number of this…
He was interviewed in Clinton, New York on September 24, 1997 by Monk Rowe, Director of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. Tim Hicks participated briefly in the interview.
We’re filming today for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive and I’m very honored to have writer and scholar Albert Murray with us. Welcome back to Hamilton.
